audit_findings.title: Serial-acquisition economics may be absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $82.578 million of 2025 acquisition cash outlay, equal to 102.7% of the $80.4 million OE anchor; $121.070 million of 2023 Scibids consideration
audit_findings.mechanism: OE and growth: acquired earnings enter the consolidated anchor and forecast, while recurring acquisition consideration may be excluded from the reinvestment charge and acquired-intangible amortization may be added back
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, we have completed seven acquisitions since 2018 and maintain an active pipeline of potential M&A targets and intend to continue evaluating add-on opportunities to bolster our current solutions suite and complement our organic growth initiatives.
audit_findings.explanation: The acquisition history and spending are demonstrated, but omission from OE is not. Because one year's acquisition cash outlay exceeded the entire OE anchor and management describes an active acquisition pipeline, the unresolved mismatch is large enough to materially overstate value if forecast growth depends on continued acquisitions.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct organic OE excluding Scibids and Rockerbox, identify acquired-intangible amortization added back, determine the acquisition spending required by each growth scenario, and rerun with that recurring reinvestment charged exactly once.

audit_findings.title: Finance-leased equipment may evade the capital-expenditure deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.805 million of 2025 finance-lease equipment additions, equal to 17.2% of the $80.4 million OE anchor; $19.847 million added in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: OE: noncash equipment additions replace or expand operating assets but do not appear in cash purchases of PP&E; adding back depreciation without deducting additions or equivalent principal payments inflates OE
audit_findings.evidence: Property and equipment under finance lease obligations, consisting of computer equipment, totaled $ 31.6 million and $ 17.8 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, refer to Footnote 7, Leases.
audit_findings.explanation: The finance-lease additions are demonstrated, but their omission from the OE calculation is unresolved. The 2025 amount alone is 17.2% of anchor OE, and first-half 2026 additions were still larger, so a missing capital charge is reasonably capable of materially lowering the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Trace the OE capital charge to the PP&E and finance-lease roll-forwards, reconcile 2025 additions of $13.805 million and principal payments of $4.552 million, and rerun using the economically appropriate maintenance charge without deducting both additions and principal.

audit_findings.title: Core software reinvestment is rising much faster than the earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $37.3 million capitalized in 2025 versus $20.3 million in 2024, an $17.0 million or 83.7% increase; 2025 spending equals 46.4% of the $80.4 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: OE and growth: capitalized internal-use software must be reflected as reinvestment; using amortization or an obsolete maintenance proxy would overstate current OE and forecast conversion of growth into distributable cash
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company capitalized $ 37.3 million and $ 20.3 million in internal-use software cost, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending increase and its importance to the operating platform are demonstrated; whether the full amount was deducted in the anchor is unresolved. At 46.4% of anchor OE, even a partial undercharge could materially change the owner-earnings base and terminal economics.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $37.3 million capitalized-software amount, including capitalized stock compensation, to the anchor's capex deduction; separate maintenance from expansion using project records and rerun all scenarios with a supportable continuing software-reinvestment requirement.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may not be fully distributable at face value
audit_findings.mechanism: Bridge: restricted, operationally required, or tax-leaking foreign cash would require a haircut to the $210.174 million cash add-back
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has generally not recorded a deferred tax liability for foreign withholding or other relevant taxes on the undistributed earnings from the Company’s international subsidiaries, as such earnings are considered to be indefinitely reinvested, with the exception of certain earnings connected to one of the Company’s international subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The indefinite-reinvestment tax policy is demonstrated, but the record does not identify how much of the June 2026 cash is foreign, trapped, operationally required, or taxable on upstreaming. The full bridge addition equals about $1.10 per diluted share, but the affected portion and therefore materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash balances by legal entity and jurisdiction at June 30, 2026, identify restricted and minimum operating balances, calculate applicable withholding or repatriation taxes, and rerun the bridge using the resulting distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: Volume growth is masking unit-price compression
audit_findings.magnitude: Measured Transaction Fees declined 3% in 2025, 6% in the first half of 2026, and 7% in the second quarter of 2026; advertiser revenue grew 5% in the first half despite 10% transaction-volume growth
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth and OE: declining unit fees reduce revenue captured from volume growth, while hosting and partner costs tied to transaction volume can compress incremental OE margins and undermine the 3% base and 5% bull OE-growth paths
audit_findings.evidence: Total advertiser revenue increased by $77.0 million, or 13%, driven primarily by a 15% increase in Media Transactions Measured, partially offset by a 3% decrease in Measured Transaction Fees, excluding the impact of an introductory fixed fee deal for one large customer.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated and worsening pricing trend, not merely a hypothetical risk. The filed 2026 results show that half-year advertiser revenue grew only half as quickly as transaction volume, making the assumed positive OE-growth paths materially dependent on pricing stabilization or offsetting margin improvements.
audit_findings.action: Build product- and cohort-level price and contribution-margin bridges, test the 2026 run rate for fee stabilization, and rerun OE growth using the filed 6% fee decline together with measured hosting and partner costs per transaction.

audit_findings.title: Economic concentration is hidden by the customer-count disclosure
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately 36% of 2025 revenue, or $269.4 million computed from $748.291 million of filed revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: OE and growth: platform repricing, higher revenue-sharing commissions, payment disruption, or loss of an integration could reduce revenue and margins despite diversified end-advertiser counts
audit_findings.evidence: Although no customer accounted for more than 10% of our revenue in 2025, two programmatic partner platforms collected approximately 24% and 12% each of our total revenue in 2025 on behalf of our advertiser customers using their platforms.
audit_findings.explanation: The collection-channel concentration is demonstrated and economically large, but no current repricing, termination, collection failure, or integration loss is supplied. It is therefore a forward-looking dependency to monitor rather than a demonstrated adjustment to present OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain platform-level revenue and contribution margins, commission schedules, termination and data-access rights, receivable exposure, and renewal dates; rerun sensitivities if either platform reprices, restricts access, delays payment, or signals termination.
